## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag does not take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which the project's cli-flags rule requires. This should be fixed before merge because CI sets options through the environment.

## Changes
This PR adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` and a new `is_excluded` helper. `collect` now skips any file whose base name matches a pattern and logs each skipped file. The PR also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Your new flag uses `default=[]` and never reads `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, so setting `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE='*.log'` in CI excludes nothing. This breaks the rule "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable" (`.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`). — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment will silently archive files they meant to skip. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, decide how one variable holds several patterns (for example, separated by `os.pathsep`), list the variable in the `docs/flags.md:7` row, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the variable.
